upper_canopy_tent.description: A triangular canopy or tent-like structure at the very top-center of the folio, from which the green stream descends. It has a decorative row of blue spheres/beads along its upper edge and radiating lines (possibly guy-wires or rays) extending outward. Colored blue-green at the apex. This is the origin point of the green stream body.

green_stream_body.description: A large flowing green organic form — possibly a river of life, a cosmic stream, or a plant stalk — descending from the upper_canopy_tent through the center of the folio. It is widest in the upper-middle zone (y≈250–450) where multiple nymph figures are embedded within it. It narrows as it descends toward y≈550. The stream is the primary bisecting visual anchor for lines f75r.1–28.

nymph_figures_in_stream.description: Several female nymph figures (approximately 6–8) are depicted partially submerged within or clinging to the sides of the green stream body. They appear at various vertical positions within the stream. One larger standing figure is visible near the bottom of the stream at approximately y≈500–560.

lower_nymph_pool.description: A rounded green pool or basin in the lower-right quadrant of the folio, approximately oval in shape. It contains a cluster of 3–4 nymph figures. The pool appears disconnected from the main green stream body. Its presence causes the bisection in f75r.44.

lower_nymph_figures.description: 3–4 female nymph figures depicted within the lower_nymph_pool, in various seated or standing poses. One figure appears to stand outside the pool to its right. The figures are rendered in the same style as those in the upper stream.

pb_label_zone.description: A narrow marginal column on the lower-left side of the folio containing the @Pb / +Pb label group (f75r.47–53). Seven short labels, one per line, arranged vertically.

text_blocks_mapping.description: Lines f75r.1–28 form the large bisected-column zone flanking the green_stream_body. Each line is split into a LEFT segment and RIGHT segment by the <->  marker. Lines 15, 16 are triple-split (two <-> each). Line 17 is quadruple-split (three <-> markers), corresponding to the widest point of the stream where it fans outward and the nymph figures are most numerous. From line 18 onward the stream narrows and single bisection resumes.
